findings.problem: fs::read_to_string performs file I/O fused with parsing and domain construction inside a single pure-looking function
findings.failure_mode: imperative-shell logic leaks into the calculation layer, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and unable to inject mock data or fail with typed errors
findings.fix: split into a shell function that reads text and a pure calculation function that parses an &[str] or Iterator<&str> into Records

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input aborts the process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use .map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or similar typed error, no unwrap

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value in the second CSV column
findings.failure_mode: hostile or malformed CSV input aborts the process instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| Error::Parse(value_str, e)) or return Result, no unwrap

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index 0 of a split result with no length guard — if line has zero bytes it panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.failure_mode: empty or whitespace-only lines panic the process
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern match on Some((name, value_str)) or return None/Error for malformed lines

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 of a split result with no length guard — lines with only one comma-separated field panic
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines (missing value column) panic instead of yielding a typed Invalid error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') which yields exactly two parts, removing the need for indexed access

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast — any u32 value > 65535 silently truncates to u16
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 silently becomes 4464, corrupting domain data without any error or warning
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow(name, parsed_u32)) instead of as cast

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside what should be pure parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure calculation layer leaks side effects, making output non-deterministic and contaminating the functional core
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the calculation layer; logging belongs in the imperative shell that calls the parser

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() unconditionally collects all split parts into Vec<String> with no domain cap or try_reserve
findings.failure_mode: a single extremely long line or a file with millions of lines causes unbounded heap growth and potential OOM
findings.fix: use split_once(',') for one-separator grammar; collect into a bounded structure or use try_reserve(validated_cap) after counting with a domain cap; push with bounds checking

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String (raw primitive) instead of a newtyped domain identifier; status/lifecycle booleans absent but name is an unvalidated string
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with empty, null-byte, or otherwise hostile strings; illegal names cannot be rejected at the boundary
findings.fix: introduce a newtype PacketName(String) or similar with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and rejects hostile input, returning a typed error

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no Result — all errors are silenced by unwrap panics rather than returned via a typed error enum
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish I/O errors from parse errors from overflow errors; no graceful recovery is possible
findings.fix: define enum Error { Io(std::io::Error), EmptyLine(usize), Invalid(usize), Overflow(String, u32), Parse(String, std::num::ParseIntError), Allocation } and return Result<Vec<Record>, Error>

findings.problem: The closure passed to .map() panics indirectly via unwrap() and indexing — even if the outer function returned Result, the closure itself has no way to propagate errors
findings.failure_mode: clippy::panic_in_result_fn: any unwrap inside the iterator chain panics the whole function instead of bubbling an error
findings.fix: change .map() to .map(...) returning Result<Record, Error>, then use .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>() to collapse into a single Result at the end

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists; the function allocates a Vec<String> per line and collects into Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: unknown performance characteristics; unbounded Vec allocation per line is wasteful when only two fields are needed
findings.fix: add a benchmark with a realistic CSV workload; replace per-line Vec allocation with split_once and borrowed str references

findings.problem: no test targets, no benchmark targets, and no CI gate exist for this crate
findings.failure_mode: no automated verification that the code compiles, passes lint gates, or behaves correctly on hostile inputs
findings.fix: add tests for valid input, empty file, malformed lines, oversized values, and missing files; add clippy and fmt gates

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() allocates a new String for every split part, then parts[0] and parts[1] clone them — the intermediate Vec<String> is fully materialized
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations on every line; memory bandwidth wasted on values that are immediately cloned again
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get (&str, &str), then use the borrows directly without intermediate allocation; only .to_string() when storing into the Record's String field

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any stated or implied performance claim
no profiler data exists to identify the actual bottleneck
no allocation tracing evidence (e.g., afl, valgrind, or custom alloc hooks)
no second-ring command evidence (no clippy, no cargo test, no cargo fmt --check)
no command-truth evidence: the function claims to load packets but no tests verify correct parsing of valid, edge, and hostile inputs
residual_risk: static review only — no commands were run (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test). All findings are based on source-level analysis. The code violates 11 absolute Holzman Rust laws including no-unsafe, no-panic, no-hidden-IO, no-lossy-cast, no-unchecked-access, and bounded-allocation. This crate cannot pass any strict lint gate as written.
